LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_nonneg: For any joint law on two finite alphabets, the mutual information between the two coordinates is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGiv: For finite-valued A, the entropy of A conditional on a value B = b is nonnegative whenever that value has positive probability. The fiber entropy is defined to be zero at all b with zero probability.
If A has a finite alphabet and Pr(B = b) > 0, the entropy of A given B = b is zero exactly when its conditional law puts probability one on a single value a.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_nonne: For a finite joint law of (A,B), the average conditional entropy H(A | B) is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_non: For any finite-valued random variables X and Y on a common source, the conditional entropy H(X | Y) is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_ze: For a finite joint law of (A,B), H(A | B) = 0 exactly when there is a function f such that a = f(b) for every pair (a,b) of positive probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_eq_: For finite-valued X and Y, H(X | Y) = 0 exactly when there exists f with X(ω) = f(Y(ω)) at every outcome ω of positive source probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_com: For a finite-valued variable Y and a function f with finite codomain, H(f(Y) | Y) = 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_sel: For any finite-valued random variable X, conditioning X on itself gives H(X | X) = 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_entrop: For a finite joint law of (A,B), H(A,B) = H(B) if and only if some function f satisfies a = f(b) for every pair (a,b) of positive joint probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_eq: For finite-valued X and Y, H(X,Y) = H(Y) exactly when X(ω) = f(Y(ω)) on every positive-probability source outcome, for one function f.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_le: If f maps one finite alphabet to another, applying f to a law p produces an output law whose entropy is at most H(p).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_eq_if: For a law p on a finite alphabet and a map f into another finite alphabet, the output has entropy H(p) exactly when f takes distinct values on every pair of distinct positive-probability inputs.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_comp_le: If X and f(X) have finite alphabets, applying the function f cannot increase entropy: H(f(X)) ≤ H(X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_comp_eq: For finite alphabets, H(f(X)) = H(X) exactly when f is injective on the set of values that X takes with positive probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_det: For finite-valued X and Z and a finite-valued function f of X, H(X | Z) = H(f(X) | Z) + H(X | f(X),Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_com: For finite alphabets and deterministic f, H(f(X) | Z) ≤ H(X | Z). Processing X can only reduce the residual uncertainty given Z.
For finite alphabets, H(f(X) | Z) = H(X | Z) if and only if a function g recovers X as g(f(X),Z) on every positive-probability source outcome.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_map_f: For a finite joint law of (A,C) and a map f of its first coordinate into a finite alphabet, H(f(A) | C) ≤ H(A | C).
For a finite pair (A,C) and a map f into a finite alphabet, H(f(A) | C) = H(A | C) exactly when some function g satisfies g(f(a),c) = a on every positive-probability pair (a,c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_le_en: For every finite joint law of (A,B), conditioning on B reduces the entropy of A: H(A | B) ≤ H(A).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_le_ent: For every finite joint law of (A,B), I(A;B) ≤ H(A), the entropy of the first marginal.
For every finite joint law of (A,B), I(A;B) ≤ H(B), the entropy of the second marginal.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_fstMargin: For a finite joint law of (A,B), the first marginal has entropy at most the joint entropy: H(A) ≤ H(A,B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_sndMargin: For a finite joint law of (A,B), the second marginal has entropy at most the joint entropy: H(B) ≤ H(A,B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_entrop: For a finite joint law of (A,B), H(A,B) ≤ H(A) + H(B). The marginals need not be independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_le_: For finite-valued random variables X and Y on a common source, H(X | Y) ≤ H(X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_le_e: For finite-valued random variables X and Y on a common source, their mutual information satisfies I(X;Y) ≤ H(X).
For finite-valued random variables X and Y on a common source, their mutual information satisfies I(X;Y) ≤ H(Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_le_join: For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy of X satisfies H(X) ≤ H(X,Y).
For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy of Y satisfies H(Y) ≤ H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_le: The joint entropy of finite-valued random variables X and Y is at most the sum of their entropies: H(X,Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_le_en: For every finite joint law of (A,B), conditioning on B reduces the entropy of A: H(A | B) ≤ H(A).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_le_ent: For every finite joint law of (A,B), I(A;B) ≤ H(A), the entropy of the first marginal.
For every finite joint law of (A,B), I(A;B) ≤ H(B), the entropy of the second marginal.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_left_le_j: For a finite joint law of (A,B), the first marginal has entropy at most the joint entropy: H(A) ≤ H(A,B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_right_le_: For a finite joint law of (A,B), the second marginal has entropy at most the joint entropy: H(B) ≤ H(A,B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropy_le_a: For a finite joint law of (A,B), H(A,B) ≤ H(A) + H(B). The marginals need not be independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_left_le: For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy of X satisfies H(X) ≤ H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_right_l: For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy of Y satisfies H(Y) ≤ H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_le: The joint entropy of finite-valued random variables X and Y is at most the sum of their entropies: H(X,Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFst: For finite-valued A and B, the mutual information computed under the conditional law given C = c is nonnegative whenever Pr(C = c) > 0. The fiber quantity is defined to be zero on null conditioning values.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_no: For every joint law of a finite triple (A,B,C), the conditional mutual information I(A;B | C) is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z with any common source law, I(X;Y | Z) ≥ 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_fstTh: If one first takes the (A,C) marginal of the joint law of (A,B,C) and then its A marginal, the result is the original A marginal.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_eq_sn: View the joint law of (A,B,C) as the law of the pair (A,(B,C)). Its second marginal is precisely the joint law of (B,C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_chain_: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), the information A shares with the pair (B,C) satisfies I(A;B,C) = I(A;C) + I(A;B | C).
For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), the chain rule in the other order is I(A;B,C) = I(A;B) + I(A;C | B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_chai: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, I(X;Y,Z) = I(X;Z) + I(X;Y | Z). The first term measures the information supplied by Z alone.
For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, I(X;Y,Z) = I(X;Y) + I(X;Z | Y). The first term measures the information supplied by Y alone.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_dete: For a finite-valued pair (X,Y) and finite-valued statistic f(X), I(X;Y) = I(f(X);Y) + I(X;Y | f(X)).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_comp: For finite alphabets, applying a deterministic function to X gives I(f(X);Y) ≤ I(X;Y).
For finite alphabets, applying a deterministic function to Y gives I(X;f(Y)) ≤ I(X;Y).
For finite alphabets and deterministic functions f and g, I(f(X);g(Y)) ≤ I(X;Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_fs: For a finite joint law of (A,B), pushing its first coordinate through a map f into a finite alphabet gives I(f(A);B) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_sn: For a finite joint law of (A,B), pushing its second coordinate through a map f into a finite alphabet gives I(A;f(B)) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_pr: For a finite joint law of (A,B), sending the two coordinates through maps f and g into finite alphabets gives I(f(A);g(B)) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_comp: For finite alphabets and deterministic functions f and g, I(f(X);g(Y)) ≤ I(X;Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_le: For a finite joint law of (A,B), pushing its first coordinate through a map f into a finite alphabet gives I(f(A);B) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_ri: For a finite joint law of (A,B), pushing its second coordinate through a map f into a finite alphabet gives I(A;f(B)) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_bo: For a finite joint law of (A,B), sending the two coordinates through maps f and g into finite alphabets gives I(f(A);g(B)) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), I(A;B | C) = H(A | C) − H(A | B,C). It measures the further reduction in uncertainty about A from observing B after C.
For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), I(A;B | C) = H(B | C) − H(B | A,C). It measures the further reduction in uncertainty about B from observing A after C.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_le_co: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), H(A | B,C) ≤ H(A | C). Observing B in addition to C can only reduce the conditional entropy of A.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_pai: For finite-valued X,Y,Z on a common source, H(X | Y,Z) ≤ H(X | Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_le: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), the conditional mutual information satisfies I(A;B | C) ≤ H(A | C).
For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), the conditional mutual information satisfies I(A;B | C) ≤ H(B | C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fstTh: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), H(A | C) ≤ H(A,B | C). After conditioning on C, the pair has at least as much entropy as its first coordinate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_sndTh: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), H(B | C) ≤ H(A,B | C). After conditioning on C, the pair has at least as much entropy as its second coordinate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pairT: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), conditional joint entropy is subadditive: H(A,B | C) ≤ H(A | C) + H(B | C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, the conditional mutual information I(X;Y | Z) is at most H(X | Z).
For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, the conditional mutual information I(X;Y | Z) is at most H(Y | Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_le_: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, H(X | Z) ≤ H(X,Y | Z), where the right side is the uncertainty of the pair given Z.
For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, H(Y | Z) ≤ H(X,Y | Z), where the right side is the uncertainty of the pair given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_pai: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z under the same source law, the conditional joint entropy satisfies H(X,Y | Z) ≤ H(X | Z) + H(Y | Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_le: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), the conditional mutual information satisfies I(A;B | C) ≤ H(A | C).
For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), the conditional mutual information satisfies I(A;B | C) ≤ H(B | C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_left_: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), H(A | C) ≤ H(A,B | C). After conditioning on C, the pair has at least as much entropy as its first coordinate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_right: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), H(B | C) ≤ H(A,B | C). After conditioning on C, the pair has at least as much entropy as its second coordinate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pair_: For a finite joint law of (A,B,C), conditional joint entropy is subadditive: H(A,B | C) ≤ H(A | C) + H(B | C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_lef: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, H(X | Z) ≤ H(X,Y | Z), where the right side is the uncertainty of the pair given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_rig: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z, H(Y | Z) ≤ H(X,Y | Z), where the right side is the uncertainty of the pair given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_pai: For finite-valued random variables X,Y,Z under the same source law, the conditional joint entropy satisfies H(X,Y | Z) ≤ H(X | Z) + H(Y | Z).
